'''ABC@Home''' was an educational and non-profit [[computer network|network computing]] project finding abc-triples related to the [[abc conjecture]] in [[number theory]] using the [[Berkeley Open Infrastructure for Network Computing]] (BOINC) [[volunteer computing]] platform.

In March 2011, there were more than 7,300 active participants from 114 countries with a total [[BOINC Credit System|BOINC credit]] of more than 2.9 billion, reporting about 10 [[FLOPS|teraflops]] (10 trillion operations per second) of processing power.<ref>{{citation |url=http://boincstats.com/stats/project_graph.php?pr=abc_main |title=Detailed user, host, team and country statistics with graphs for BOINC |accessdate=2011-03-11 |work=boincstats.com |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20101120150315/http://boincstats.com/stats/project_graph.php?pr=abc_main |archivedate=2010-11-20 }}</ref>

In 2011, the project met its goal of finding all abc-triples of at most 18 digits. By 2015, the project had found 23.8 million triples in total, and ceased operations soon after.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.math.leidenuniv.nl/~desmit/abc/index.php?set=1 |title=ABC Triples |last=de Smit |first=Bart |accessdate=2017-03-09 |archive-date=2016-12-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161204235137/http://www.math.leidenuniv.nl/~desmit/abc/index.php?set=1 |url-status=live }}</ref>
